sentences: On a summer afternoon, a sudden shower pours down on a great bridge in Edo.
People hurry across under straw hats, umbrellas and matting held over their heads, while the far bank fades into grey shapes behind the rain.
Hiroshige cut the rain as two layers of fine lines, black and grey, set at slightly different angles, so the downpour seems to shift in the wind.
The bridge itself is cropped and seen at a steep angle from above, a daring composition for its time.
The print is number 58 in the series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo and was published in the ninth month of 1857.
Thirty years later in Paris, Van Gogh copied it in oils and even framed his copy with a border of Japanese characters borrowed from other prints.
